key_insight: AeroZoo shows that encoding boundary conditions sharply improves aerodynamic flow predictions, while generalizing to unseen enclosures and boundary-condition layouts remains difficult.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests whether fast CFD surrogates can handle new shapes and flow domains rather than only variations within one design family.
method: Generate 3,815 time-mean unsteady RANS solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from 10³ to 10⁸.
Represent each PDE problem using boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values and fluid properties.
Evaluate two tasks using engineering metrics and 22 frozen, geometry-disjoint splits.
evidence_signal: On the 2,816-sample stable-mean benchmark, boundary-condition tokens reduced GeoTransolver’s random-split median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of inlet speed in single-seed runs; ISLA reached 5.3% over four seeds.
watch_item: Held-out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts increased ISLA’s error 2.4–9.2 times, cautioning against assuming reliable deployment beyond training conditions.
paper_title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
